title: Alphen aan den Rijn sword blade inscription (Archeon)

steps.what: van Hasselt, van Halteren, Peters on the Alphen blade: partial Latin expansions, rest unread; transcriptions differ.
Vowels 12/38 face A, 17/41 face B; repeat MTINIUSCSD across faces; DIO x2, DIC x3.
Checked for a substitution: none indicated; text is Latin-like invocation with abbreviations and garbled letters. No expansion of the remainder is testable.
lm.best_language on both faces: Latin ranks first (-4.06/char) but only narrowly over French; no sign of substitution.
Found the Madoc 2014 article (Archeon PDF) with photographs and a transcription drawn from them, and Wagner et al. 2009 / Wagner 2013 on Uppsala DiVA.
Took van Hasselt's drawing as the text (replacing forum transcriptions); checked against the published photographs.
Aligned both faces to the Wagner/Worley readings of siblings: ISSCSD shared with Fyris 74, OXMTINIUS with W 1830, BENED with the Finnish sword.

Segmented both faces with the SDX-family expansions (SCS D = Sanctus Dominus, X = Christus, IS = Iesus, MTINIUS = Martinius): 56 of 79 (71%) letters fall in formula elements; the rest unexplained and the expansions are the sibling authors' tentative ones.

outcome.method_basis: No key exists: the text is an invocation in abbreviations. A family-level parse (56 of 79 (71%) letters in formula elements, using sibling authors' expansions) is not a decipherment; the rest has no accepted expansion.
outcome.notes: Formula-level parse from the SDX family; remaining groups need the conservation report and an agreed expansion of the formulae.

prior.where: van Hasselt 2014 (BENED, SCS, MTINIUS as Martinius); Wagner et al. 2009 and 2013 read the sibling family (SCS D X = Sanctus Dominus Christus); nobody has read Alphen as a whole.

human: Set the goal "solve the cipher behind the Alphen aan den Rijn Sword Inscription"; no target-specific intervention recorded.
